verdict.rationale: WooCommerce's first-party Storefront docs describe add_action() hooks that let developers insert PHP into core templates, so in-platform hook-based code injection exists. The only evidence, however, concerns template and content insertion, not backend commerce logic. Outbound webhooks and the marketplace extensions are not this capability and earn no credit. Missing for 10: documented hooks or filters for discounts, shipping-rate rules and checkout validation, any serverless function runtime, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can inject custom backend logic — discounts, shipping rules, validation — as serverless functions or hooks that run inside the platform

citations.quote: Storefront has a lot of add_action() functions... These allow you to insert sections of content using HTML, PHP, Javascript into its core templates.
